Campaign angle notes:

- Legal has approved all four angles: price cut (A), quality story (B), limited-time urgency (C), and customer testimonial (D).
- Across 10 pushes, 5 landed (50%). Analytics provides no per-day or per-angle breakdown, so no angle has demonstrated superiority.
- Usage so far: D customer testimonial 5 times; B quality story 4 times; C urgency once; A price cut not tested.
- Customer testimonials and quality stories were favored to build trust and durable appeal without discounting or pressure, but this is a strategic preference, not evidence of better performance.
- Two-subscribe events reported on multiple days were already processed and offer no actionable angle-level feedback. Do not change strategy based on them alone.
- No deliverability complaints were reported.
- List growth and refreshed creative are contextual signals only; they do not establish which angle works.
- Continue collecting angle-level results. Prioritize a balanced test, including A and C, before drawing conclusions.

Campaign angle notes:

- Legal has approved all four angles: price cut (A), quality story (B), limited-time urgency (C), and customer testimonial (D).
- Across the first 10 pushes, 5 landed (50%); analytics provided no per-day or angle-level breakdown.
- The next 10 pushes (Days 11–20) all used A, and analytics reports 0 of 10 landed. This is a concerning signal for A, but lacks per-day detail and should not be treated as definitive without comparable testing.
- Current usage: A price cut 10 times; D customer testimonial 5 times; B quality story 4 times; C urgency once. Overall, 5 of the first 10 landed, followed by 0 of the next 10; do not pool this as proof of angle superiority because conditions and creative may differ.
- Testimonials and quality stories remain strategic preferences for trust and durable appeal, not evidence-backed winners.
- Two-subscribe events and support-reported unsubscribes were already processed; they provide no actionable angle-level feedback. Do not change strategy based on them alone.
- No deliverability complaints were reported.
- List growth and refreshed banner art are contextual signals only; they do not establish which angle works.
- Stop repeatedly pushing A. Resume a balanced test across B, C, and D, with A included as a controlled comparison if needed. Collect angle-level results and avoid conclusions until comparable data and breakdowns are available.

Campaign angle notes:

- Legal has approved all four angles: A price cut, B quality story, C limited-time urgency, and D customer testimonial.
- Through Day 30: 30 pushes total. A used 10 times, B 12 times, C 3 times, D 5 times.
- Results by period: first 10 pushes had 5 land (50%); Days 11–20 used A exclusively and had 0 of 10 land; Days 21–30 had 5 of 10 land. Analytics provides no per-day or angle-level breakdown, so none of these periods proves angle superiority.
- Days 21–30 were heavily concentrated on B (8 pushes) with C twice. The reported 5/10 result cannot be assigned to B or C individually. Day 29’s actual push was C; ignore the contradictory note suggesting a B/D comparison.
- Stop repeatedly pushing A; its 0/10 block is concerning but not definitive without comparable testing and creative/context controls.
- B and D remain strategic preferences for trust and durable appeal, not proven winners. C has insufficient data.
- Resume a genuinely balanced or randomized test across A–D, avoiding another long run of one angle. Record exact angle, creative, date, and per-push outcome; request angle-level analytics before drawing conclusions.
- Support-reported unsubscribes, two-subscribe events, list growth, refreshed banner art, legal sign-off, and absence of deliverability complaints are contextual only. They do not establish angle performance or justify strategy changes alone.

Campaign angle notes:

- Through Day 30: 30 pushes total—A 10, B 12, C 3, D 5. First 10: 5/10 landed; Days 11–20: A exclusively, 0/10; Days 21–30: 5/10, mostly B (8 pushes) plus C (2). No angle-level or per-day analytics, so these periods do not establish superiority. Day 29 was C; ignore the contradictory B/D note.
- Days 31–40 added B twice, C three times, and D five times; A was not used. Analytics reports 0/10 landed across the latest block, but provides no per-day breakdown, so this cannot be attributed to D or any other angle.
- Do not repeatedly push A; its 0/10 block is concerning but not definitive without comparable testing and controls. Likewise, B and D are strategic preferences for trust and durable appeal, not proven winners; C remains under-tested.

- Through Day 30: 30 pushes—A 10, B 12, C 3, D 5. First 10: 5/10 landed; Days 11–20: A exclusively, 0/10; Days 21–30: 5/10, mostly B (8 pushes) plus C (2). No angle-level or per-day analytics, so these periods do not establish superiority. Day 29 was C; ignore the contradictory B/D note.

- Do not repeatedly push A; its 0/10 block is concerning but not definitive without comparable testing and controls. B and D remain strategic preferences for trust and durable appeal, not proven winners. C is no longer entirely untested but still needs controlled comparison.
- Continue a balanced/randomized A–D test rather than choosing an angle from aggregate blocks alone. Record exact angle, creative/banner version, date, and outcome for every push; request angle- and creative-level analytics.
- Unsubscribes, list growth, banner refreshes, legal approval, support events, and lack of deliverability complaints are contextual only; they do not establish angle performance or justify strategy changes.

Campaign angle notes:

- Legal has approved all four angles: A) price cut, B) quality story, C) limited-time urgency, D) customer testimonial.
- Through Day 30: 30 pushes—A 10, B 12, C 3, D 5. First 10: 5/10 landed; Days 11–20: A exclusively, 0/10; Days 21–30: 5/10, mostly B (8 pushes) plus C (2). No angle-level or per-day analytics, so these blocks do not establish superiority. Day 29 was C; ignore the contradictory B/D note.
- Days 31–40: B twice, C three times, D five times; A not used. Block reported 0/10, with no per-day breakdown.
- Days 41–50: C exclusively, including a banner-art refresh on Day 42. Reported 2/10 landed, without per-day or creative-level breakdown. This is limited evidence C can perform, not proof it is superior or that the banner helped.
- Days 51–60: D exclusively; reported 5/10 landed. Three banner-art refreshes occurred during this block, but no per-day or creative-level data exists, so results cannot be attributed confidently to D or the refreshed art.
- A’s 0/10 block is concerning but not definitive. B and D remain strategic preferences for trust and durable appeal, not proven winners. C has some evidence but still needs controlled comparison.
- Resume a balanced/randomized A–D test; avoid another long single-angle block. Record exact angle, testimonial/creative and banner version, date, and outcome for every push. Request angle- and creative-level analytics.
- Unsubscribes, list growth, banner refreshes, legal approval, support events, and lack of deliverability complaints are contextual only; they do not establish angle performance or justify strategy changes.
